mainTopic: Laws of the עיר הנדחת (tithe, holy writings, rebuilding, trees), the curse on rebuilding יריחו, and אליהו and the key to rain
overview: The גמרא first asks why the מעשר שני of an עיר הנדחת must be hidden away instead of redeemed. It explains this with רבא's rule that the walls of ירושלים 'absorb' the tithe only by rabbinic law, and only while the walls are standing. Next it notes that the משנה's rule about holy writings does not follow רבי אליעזר, who holds that a city with even one מזוזה cannot become an עיר הנדחת. The גמרא suggests that the argument over turning the ruined city into gardens depends on רבי אבין's rule. It rejects that suggestion and says the real argument is over the word ״עוד״. A ברייתא about trees then leads to יריחו, which may never be rebuilt under any name. The story of חיאל, who lost all his sons for rebuilding it, follows. אחאב mocks the curse, so אליהו stops the rain and receives its key. Later he has to give the key back to ה׳ in exchange for the key to תחיית המתים. The amud ends as רבי יוסי begins a teaching about אליהו that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not redeem the impure tithe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: if this מעשר שני became impure, it should simply be redeemed, as another משנה teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why hide it away? Let him redeem it! After all, a משנה teaches that something bought with מעשר שני money that became impure may be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the explanation of the משנה that says the מעשר שני of an עיר הנדחת must be hidden away (גניזה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we are talking about food bought with מעשר שני money that became impure, there is a known rule that it can be redeemed. So why does our משנה say it has to be hidden away?

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, which must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
Something bought with מעשר שני money

phrases.english: And let him redeem it,
as we learned in a mishnah:
an item bought with second-tithe money that became impure
shall be redeemed.

steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the משנה's מעשר שני must be hidden away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that impure items bought with מעשר שני money are redeemed, so hiding them away seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our משנה follows רבי יהודה, who says such an item is buried, not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is like רבי יהודה, who says an impure item bought with מעשר שני money must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying our משנה follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה that said 'redeem it' is not the only view. רבי יהודה says such an item must be buried, so our משנה's ruling to hide it away fits his opinion.

phrases.english: It is according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: it shall be buried.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The impure item should be redeemed, as the other משנה says.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה, it is buried, which matches our משנה.

steps.title: Then why mention the idolatrous city?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if this is just רבי יהודה's general rule, why does the משנה connect it to an עיר הנדחת?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the משנה mention an עיר הנדחת specifically? The same rule would apply to any city!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason for hiding it away is only that it is impure, as רבי יהודה says, then the rule has nothing to do with an עיר הנדחת. But the משנה clearly treats this as a special law of the עיר הנדחת.

keyTerms.meaning: A city that was led into idol worship and must be destroyed
Of the general world, an ordinary case

phrases.english: If so,
why specifically an idolatrous city?
Even an ordinary one too!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה follows רבי יהודה about impure items
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule applies everywhere, so it makes no sense for the משנה to tie it to an עיר הנדחת.

steps.title: New case: pure tithe, and the walls fell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the case. The tithe is pure, it was brought into ירושלים, and then the walls of ירושלים fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really the משנה is talking about pure מעשר שני, in a case where the walls of ירושלים fell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea that the tithe was impure and gives a new picture of the case. The next step will explain why the walls matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the tithe is pure, so impurity is no longer the reason it cannot be redeemed. Because the walls fell, the tithe is not stuck with the special status that entering ירושלים normally gives. So it stays part of the spoils of the עיר הנדחת, and that is why it must be hidden away.

keyTerms.meaning: Walls, here the walls of ירושלים

phrases.english: Rather, it is actually talking about pure tithe,
for example, where the walls fell,
phrases.notes: The walls of ירושלים fell after the tithe had already been brought inside.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is about impure tithe, following רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is about pure tithe in ירושלים after its walls fell, which is unique to an עיר הנדחת.

steps.title: רבא's rule about the walls of Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that the walls allowing tithe to be eaten is from the תורה. The walls 'absorbing' tithe so it can no longer be redeemed is only a rabbinic rule, and it applies only while the walls are standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבא. He said: the wall's power to let you eat the tithe is from the תורה. Its power to 'absorb' the tithe is only rabbinic. The Rabbis made that decree only when the walls are standing, not when they are down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's rule to explain why fallen walls change the outcome in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once מעשר שני enters ירושלים, it is 'absorbed' and can no longer be redeemed. That rule is only rabbinic, and the Rabbis never applied it when the walls are down. So the tithe of the עיר הנדחת keeps its status as the city's spoils and must be hidden away.

keyTerms.meaning: To absorb or 'capture', so the tithe can no longer be redeemed once inside

steps.whatToRemember: The power of the walls of ירושלים to 'absorb' מעשר שני is only rabbinic and works only while the walls stand. That is why tithe from an עיר הנדחת, in ירושלים after the walls fell, is hidden away.
steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction between the תורה-level and rabbinic powers of the walls is a general rule about מעשר שני, not only about this case.

phrases.english: and this follows Rava,
as Rava said:
the wall, for eating — is from the Torah;
for absorbing — is rabbinic.
phrases.notes: 'Absorbing' means that once the tithe is inside, it can no longer be redeemed and taken out.

phrases.english: And when the Rabbis decreed,
it was when the walls are standing;
when the walls are not there — no.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wall's power to let you eat the tithe is from the תורה. Its power to absorb the tithe is rabbinic and applies only when the walls are standing.

steps.title: Holy writings are hidden away, against רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that holy writings in an עיר הנדחת are hidden away, and notes that this does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says holy writings must be hidden away. Our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and makes a comment about it. The next step brings the source showing what רבי אליעזר holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה assumes a city with holy writings can still become an עיר הנדחת, and the writings are just hidden away instead of burned. That assumption clashes with רבי אליעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy writings, such as books of תנ״ך
They must be hidden away (put in גניזה)

phrases.english: Holy writings must be hidden away.
Our mishnah is not in line with Rabbi Eliezer,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ יִגָּנְזוּ. מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's rule that holy writings are hidden away does not follow רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: one מזוזה saves the city
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר: a city with even one מזוזה cannot become an עיר הנדחת. The whole city must be burned, and God's name may not be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: any city with even one מזוזה does not become an עיר הנדחת. The פסוק says to burn the city and all its spoils entirely, and that is impossible where there is a מזוזה, because the תורה says 'You shall not do so to ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves רבי אליעזר disagrees with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עיר הנדחת must be burned completely, including all its spoils. A מזוזה has God's name, which may not be destroyed. So if the city cannot be burned entirely, it cannot become an עיר הנדחת at all. Our משנה instead says the holy writings are simply hidden away.

keyTerms.meaning: A scroll on the doorpost with God's name

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not say the מזוזה is hidden away. He says the whole city never becomes an עיר הנדחת. That is exactly where he differs from our משנה.

phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עִיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ אֲפִילּוּ מְזוּזָה אַחַת
phrases.english: any city that has even one mezuzah
does not become an idolatrous city,
as it is said:
"And you shall burn with fire the city
and all its spoils, entirely."
phrases.notes: דברים 13:17

phrases.english: And where there is a mezuzah, that is not possible,
as it is written:
"You shall not do so to the Lord your God."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:4. This is the source that we may not destroy God's name.

steps.raayaObject: That our משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אליעזר, based on דברים 13:17 and דברים 12:4

steps.title: Is the משנה's dispute based on רבי אבין's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and suggests that the תנאים there argue over a rule taught by רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the Holy One, Blessed be He, said, and so on. Shall we say that the תנאים disagree about the teaching of רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and offers a possible reason behind the argument there. The next step quotes the rule it has in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'and so on' points to the rest of the משנה, where רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי argue about turning the ruined city into gardens and orchards. The גמרא suggests, with the word לימא ('shall we say'), that their argument rests on a rule of how to read פסוקים. This is only a proposal, and step 11 rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said, and so on.
phrases.notes: 'And so on' covers the rest of the משנה, including the argument about turning the ruined city into gardens.

phrases.english: Shall we say that about the teaching of Rabbi Avin
in the name of Rabbi Ile'a they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּדְרַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the argument in the משנה about rebuilding the ruined city depends on רבי אבין's rule.

steps.title: רבי אבין's rule: positive general, negative detail
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעא teaches that when a כלל is written as a מצות עשה and a פרט as a לא תעשה, we do not apply the rule of כלל ופרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעא: anywhere you find a כלל written as a positive command and a פרט written as a prohibition, we do not read it using the rule of כלל ופרט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rule it mentioned in the last step. This sets up the next move, where it will apply the rule to the פסוקים about the עיר הנדחת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when a כלל is followed by a פרט, the כלל is limited to the פרט. רבי אבין says this does not apply when the two parts are different kinds of commands, one positive and one negative. In that case, each part is read as its own separate law.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule followed by a detail, which limits the general rule to the detail
We do not interpret or judge it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for how to read פסוקים, and it can decide whether two clauses are one law or two separate laws.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ile'a:
Any place where you find
a general rule as a positive command and a detail as a prohibition,
we do not interpret it by the rule of "general and detail."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a כלל is written as an עשה and a פרט as a לא תעשה, the rule of כלל ופרט is not applied.

steps.title: Spelling out the suggested dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its suggestion: one תנא accepts רבי אבין's rule and the other does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: So one Sage holds like רבי אבין, and the other Sage does not hold like רבי אבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the suggestion it began in step 8. It says the two תנאים in the משנה argue over whether to accept רבי אבין's rule. This is only a proposal, and the גמרא will test it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse has a מצות עשה (״והיתה תל עולם״) and a לא תעשה (״לא תבנה עוד״). Whoever holds like רבי אבין does not read the two parts as כלל ופרט, so ״תל עולם״ stands as its own command and even gardens are forbidden. Whoever does not hold like רבי אבין limits the general phrase to the detail: only rebuilding is banned, and gardens are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage (literally 'master'), used for each side of a dispute
He does not hold / does not accept this view

phrases.english: that one Sage holds like רבי אבין,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי הגלילי, who forbids even making gardens and orchards there.

phrases.english: and the other Sage does not hold like רבי אבין.
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא, who permits gardens and orchards.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמָר אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין, וּמָר לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אבין's rule from step 9 to the dispute suggested in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא really about accepting רבי אבין's rule?

steps.title: Everyone accepts רבי אבין; they argue over the word ״עוד״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Both sides accept רבי אבין, and they argue over what ״עוד״ means.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds like רבי אבין. Here is what they argue about. One Sage holds that ״עוד״ means 'ever again, in any way.' The other holds that ״עוד״ means it may not be rebuilt the way it was before, but it may be made into gardens and orchards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion. It says the argument is not about רבי אבין at all. It is about how to read one word in the verse, ״עוד״ ('again').
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both תנאים agree on the method of reading the verse. The disagreement moves to the meaning of ״לא תבנה עוד״. For one, ״עוד״ bans any rebuilding at all, even gardens. For the other, ״עוד״ only bans restoring the city as it was, so gardens and orchards are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Again,' the word in ״לא תבנה עוד״ that the dispute turns on

steps.whatToRemember: The final explanation is that both sides accept רבי אבין. The real argument is whether ״עוד״ forbids every use of the land, or only rebuilding the city as it was.

phrases.english: No, everyone
holds like רבי אבין,
and here they argue about this:
one Sage holds that ״עוד״ means completely, never again in any way,
phrases.notes: ״עוד״ is from the verse ״לא תבנה עוד״, 'it shall not be built again.'

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds that ״עוד״ means:
it may not be built back to how it was,
but it may be made into gardens and orchards.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין, וְהָכָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 10 and moves the dispute to the meaning of one word.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the תנאים argue over רבי אבין's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained even if everyone accepts רבי אבין: they differ on the meaning of ״עוד״.

steps.title: Trees in an עיר הנדחת and in 'another city'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that cut trees in an עיר הנדחת are forbidden and growing trees are permitted. In 'another city,' all trees are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if there were trees in the city, the cut-off ones are forbidden and the ones still growing are permitted. But in 'another city,' all trees are forbidden, whether cut or growing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about trees found in an עיר הנדחת. It also mentions a special 'other city' with a stricter rule, which the גמרא will explain next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an עיר הנדחת, the ברייתא divides trees into two groups. Cut trees are forbidden and growing trees are permitted. For the 'other city' the ברייתא is stricter: there is no such split, and every tree is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached, cut off from the ground
Attached, still growing in the ground
'Another city,' a special city with a stricter rule

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: if there were trees in it,
the cut-off ones are forbidden,
the attached ones are permitted.
But the trees of another city,
whether cut-off or attached, are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the status of trees in a destroyed city.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an עיר הנדחת, cut trees are forbidden and growing trees are permitted. In 'another city,' all trees are forbidden.

steps.title: Which city is 'another city'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which city the ברייתא means by 'another city.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'another city'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about the ברייתא's words. This sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a stricter rule for 'another city' but never said which city it meant. Before the rule can be understood, the גמרא needs to know what city this is.

phrases.english: What is 'another city'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what a phrase in the ברייתא of step 12 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which city does the ברייתא call 'another city'?

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is יריחו
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that 'another city' is יריחו, which was declared חרם and cursed by יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it is יריחו. As it is written: 'The city shall be חרם to ה׳...' and 'יהושע swore at that time: cursed is the man before ה׳ who rises and builds this city, יריחו. He will lay its foundation with his firstborn, and set up its gates with his youngest son.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question: the 'other city' is יריחו. He proves it with פסוקים from ספר יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יריחו was declared חרם, fully devoted to ה׳, and יהושע cursed anyone who would rebuild it. That explains why its rule is stricter than an ordinary עיר הנדחת: everything in it is banned, even trees still growing.

keyTerms.meaning: Jericho, the first city conquered by יהושע
Devoted to ה׳, forbidden for personal use

phrases.english: רב חסדא said: יריחו,
as it is written: 'And the city shall be חרם to Hashem...'
phrases.notes: יהושע 6:17. The dots mean the גמרא jumps ahead to a later פסוק.

phrases.english: 'And יהושע swore at that time, saying:'
phrases.notes: יהושע 6:26.

phrases.english: 'Cursed is the man before ה׳'

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר יָקוּם וּבָנָה אֶת הָעִיר הַזֹּאת אֶת יְרִיחוֹ
phrases.english: 'who rises up and builds this city, יריחו;'
'with his firstborn he will lay its foundation,'
phrases.notes: This means he will lose his firstborn son when he lays the foundation.

phrases.english: 'and with his youngest he will set up its gates.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Another city' is יריחו, which was made חרם and cursed by יהושע.

steps.title: יריחו may not be rebuilt under any name
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that יריחו may not be rebuilt under another name, and no other city may be built and called יריחו. It brings the story of חיאל as its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: do not build יריחו under the name of another city, and do not build another city under the name יריחו. As it is written: 'חיאל from בית אל built יריחו. With אבירם his firstborn he laid its foundation, and with שגוב his youngest he set up its gates.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that widens the ban on building יריחו. The ban applies even if the name is changed, and to any city given the name יריחו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the name does not get around יהושע's curse. Building יריחו and calling it something else is banned, and so is building another city and calling it יריחו. The ברייתא points to חיאל, on whom the curse came true exactly as יהושע had said.

keyTerms.meaning: חיאל from בית אל, the man who rebuilt יריחו

steps.whatToRemember: יריחו is stricter than an ordinary עיר הנדחת. All its trees are forbidden, and it may never be rebuilt, not even under a different name.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: לֹא יְרִיחוֹ עַל שֵׁם עִיר אַחֶרֶת,
phrases.english: It was taught: not יריחו under the name of another city,
phrases.notes: He means: you may not build יריחו and give it a different name.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עִיר אַחֶרֶת עַל שֵׁם יְרִיחוֹ,
phrases.english: and not another city under the name of יריחו,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״בָּנָה חִיאֵל בֵּית הָאֱלִי אֶת יְרִיחֹה
phrases.english: as it is written: 'חיאל from בית אל built יריחו;'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 16:34.

phrases.english: 'with אבירם his firstborn he laid its foundation,'
'and with שגוב his youngest he set up its gates.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: לֹא יְרִיחוֹ עַל שֵׁם עִיר אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב חסדא's identification of יריחו and widens the ban on rebuilding it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יריחו may not be rebuilt under another name, and no other city may be built under the name יריחו.

steps.title: What חיאל should have learned from his sons' deaths
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that the death of אבירם, the firstborn, was not yet enough to teach a lesson, but the death of שגוב, the youngest, should have taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: with אבירם his firstborn, the wicked one did not have to learn. With שגוב his youngest, he should have learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the פסוק that describes חיאל rebuilding יריחו. It talks about when the lesson of the curse should have been clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's wording is unclear. It seems to call someone 'wicked' and says one death was not a lesson while another was. This unclear wording sets up the next question.

phrases.english: It is taught: With Abiram his firstborn,
phrases.notes: This uses the words of the פסוק about חיאל, מלכים א 16:34.

phrases.english: the wicked one did not have to learn.
With Segub his youngest, he should have learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: בַּאֲבִירָם בְּכוֹרוֹ, רָשָׁע, לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לִלְמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of חיאל brought in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the first son died, חיאל could not yet see the curse. By the time the last son died, he should have understood it.

steps.title: Who is wicked and what does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what אבירם and שגוב did wrong, and what the ברייתא is really saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did אבירם and שגוב do? What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is confused by the ברייתא's wording and asks for an explanation. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the word 'רשע' seems to describe the son אבירם, but the sons did nothing wrong. So the גמרא asks what the ברייתא actually means.

phrases.english: What did Abiram and Segub do?
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's wording seems to call the sons wicked, which makes no sense.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבִירָם וּשְׂגוּב מַאי עֲבוּד? מַאי קָאָמַר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the 'רשע' is and what the ברייתא means.

steps.title: The wicked one is חיאל, who should have learned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: from אבירם's death, the wicked חיאל should have understood what would happen with שגוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: from אבירם his firstborn, that wicked man should have learned, before it came to שגוב his youngest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא. The 'wicked one' is חיאל, not his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the reading is fixed, the problem disappears. The sons did nothing wrong. Their father חיאל should have seen the curse working and stopped before he lost all his sons.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
From Abiram his firstborn he should have learned
that wicked man, about Segub his youngest.
phrases.notes: The wicked man is חיאל himself, not his sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: בַּאֲבִירָם בְּכוֹרוֹ הָיָה לוֹ לִלְמוֹד לְאוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רשע is חיאל. From the death of his firstborn, he should have understood that the curse would take all his sons, down to שגוב.

steps.title: He buried his sons one after another
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק names שגוב as the youngest even though that seems obvious. This teaches that חיאל kept burying sons, one by one, from אבירם down to שגוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says 'with אבירם his firstborn,' don't I already know that שגוב was his youngest? Why does it say 'שגוב his youngest'? It teaches that he kept burying sons, from אבירם until שגוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an extra-looking phrase in the פסוק and learns from it that all of חיאל's sons died gradually.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they all died gradually, חיאל had plenty of warning. This backs up the reading in step 18 that he should have learned.

keyTerms.meaning: why does the פסוק need to say it?

phrases.english: From the fact that it says "with Abiram his firstborn"
do I not know that Segub was his youngest?
Why does the verse say "Segub his youngest"?
It teaches that he kept on burying
from Abiram until Segub.
phrases.notes: So all the sons in between died too, one at a time.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּשְׁמָע שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״בַּאֲבִירָם בְּכוֹרוֹ״ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁשְּׂגוּב צְעִירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 18 by showing from the פסוק that חיאל had ongoing warning.
steps.raayaObject: That חיאל should have learned from his sons' deaths.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra-looking words 'שגוב צעירו' in the פסוק.

steps.title: At the house of mourning, חיאל wonders about the curse
steps.stepSummary: אחאב, חיאל's close friend, comes with אליהו to comfort him. חיאל asks whether יהושע's curse really covered rebuilding יריחו under any name.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחאב was his groomsman. He and אליהו came to ask about his welfare at the house of mourning. He sat and said: perhaps when יהושע cursed, this is what he cursed: not to build יריחו under another city's name, and not to build another city under the name יריחו?
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. It sets the scene of the visit, and חיאל asks a question about what the curse covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חיאל is now facing the result of his actions. He asks whether the wide curse taught in step 15 is what caused his loss. This sets up אליהו's answer.

phrases.english: Ahab was his groomsman.
He and Elijah came
to ask about his welfare at the house of mourning.
He sat and said:
phrases.notes: The one speaking is חיאל, the mourner.

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא כִּי לָט יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָכִי לָט –
phrases.english: Perhaps when Joshua cursed, this is how he cursed:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְרִיחוֹ עַל שֵׁם עִיר אַחֶרֶת,
phrases.english: not Jericho under the name of another city,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עִיר אַחֶרֶת עַל שֵׁם יְרִיחוֹ?
phrases.english: and not another city under the name of Jericho?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the חיאל story with the visit after his sons died.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether יהושע's curse covered building יריחו under any name.

steps.title: אליהו confirms the curse
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers: yes, that is the curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו confirms that יהושע's curse covered this case, which explains חיאל's loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This short answer ties חיאל's tragedy directly to יהושע's curse. It also prompts אחאב's objection in the next step.

phrases.english: Elijah said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers חיאל's question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the curse was exactly that.

steps.title: אחאב mocks: משה's curse isn't happening, so why would יהושע's?
steps.stepSummary: אחאב argues that משה warned idol worship would stop the rain. Yet אחאב put an idol on every furrow, and the rain is so heavy he can't get out to worship. So how could the curse of יהושע, משה's student, come true?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: now, the curse of משה is not being fulfilled, as it is written 'and you go astray and worship...' and it is written 'God's anger will burn against you and He will shut the heavens...' That man set up idols on every single furrow, and the rain doesn't let him go and bow to them. Will the curse of יהושע, his student, be fulfilled?
steps.whatsHappening: אחאב challenges אליהו. He uses a 'teacher versus student' argument to mock the idea that יהושע's curse caused חיאל's loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is a קל וחומר. If even the teacher's curse, written in the תורה, is not coming true, the student's curse surely won't. אחאב points to his own idol worship and the plentiful rain as proof.

phrases.english: He said to him: Now, the curse of Moses
phrases.notes: אחאב is the speaker here, talking to אליהו.

phrases.english: is not being fulfilled,
as it is written: "And you go astray and worship..."
phrases.notes: דברים 11:16

phrases.english: and it is written: "Then God's anger will burn against you
and He will shut the heavens..."
phrases.notes: דברים 11:17

phrases.aramaic: וְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא אוֹקֵים לֵיהּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
phrases.english: and that man set up idol worship
phrases.notes: 'That man' is אחאב's way of talking about himself.

phrases.english: on every single furrow
and the rain does not let him
go and bow down to it.
Will the curse of Joshua, his student, be fulfilled?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא לְוָוטְתָא דְּמֹשֶׁה לָא קָא מִקַּיְימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אליהו's confirmation in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יהושע's curse caused חיאל's sons to die.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from teacher to student: משה's curse, that idol worship would stop the rain, is not happening, so יהושע's curse should not happen either.

steps.title: אליהו stops the rain and receives its key
steps.stepSummary: Right away, אליהו swears there will be no dew or rain. He prays, receives the key to rainfall, and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately: 'And אליהו the Tishbite, from the settlers of Gilead, said: As the Lord God of Israel lives, there shall be no dew or rain...' He prayed for mercy, they gave him the key of rain, and he got up and went.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers אחאב's mockery with action. He makes משה's curse come true by stopping the rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחאב's whole proof was the plentiful rain. Once the rain stops, משה's curse is clearly being fulfilled, and his argument falls apart. That shows יהושע's curse is real too.
steps.whatToRemember: The curses of משה and יהושע both come true. חיאל lost his sons for rebuilding יריחו, and אליהו stopped the rain to answer אחאב's mockery.

phrases.english: Immediately: "And Elijah the Tishbite said,
of the settlers of Gilead,
As the Lord God of Israel lives,
there shall be no dew or rain..."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 17:1. In an oath like this, 'אם' means 'there will not be.'

phrases.english: He prayed for mercy,
and they gave him the key of rain,
and he got up and went.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אחאב's challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Answer by action: the curse is shown to be real.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אחאב thought the heavy rain proved that משה's curse was not working.
steps.terutzMaskana: אליהו stops the rain, which makes משה's curse visibly come true and defeats אחאב's argument.

steps.title: ה׳ sends אליהו to hide, and ravens feed him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוקים‎: ה׳ tells אליהו to hide by נחל כרית, and ravens bring him bread and meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ told אליהו: go east and hide by נחל כרית. Ravens brought him bread and meat every morning.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that אליהו holds the key to rain, the גמרא continues the story by quoting the פסוקים. This sets up a question about where the ravens' food came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו has just stopped the rain. ה׳ moves him to a hidden place and feeds him there in a miraculous way. The detail of the ravens' food is what the גמרא will ask about next.

keyTerms.meaning: Wadi Cherith, a stream where אליהו hid

phrases.english: "And the word of ה׳ came to him, saying:
phrases.notes: מלכים א 17:2–3, 6

phrases.english: Go from here and turn eastward,
and hide yourself by Wadi Cherith."
"And the ravens brought him
bread and meat in the morning, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיְהִי דְבַר ה׳ אֵלָיו לֵאמֹר לֵךְ מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after אליהו took the key to rain and left.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק says ravens fed אליהו while he hid at נחל כרית.

steps.title: Where did the ravens get the food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the bread and meat came from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where did they bring it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the פסוק: where did the ravens get the bread and meat?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the ravens brought food but does not say where it came from. The גמרא wants to fill in that missing detail.

phrases.english: From where?
phrases.notes: He means: from where did the ravens bring the bread and meat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the ravens' bread and meat.

steps.title: From אחאב's slaughterhouse
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב answers that the food came from אחאב's slaughterhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: from the butchers of אחאב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, quoting רב, answers the question: the ravens took the food from אחאב's slaughterhouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food that kept אליהו alive came from the house of the wicked king אחאב, the same king he was punishing with the drought.

keyTerms.meaning: The slaughterhouse, the place of the butchers

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
From the slaughterhouse of Ahab.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ravens brought the food from אחאב's slaughterhouse.

steps.title: The stream dries up and ה׳ sends אליהו to צרפת
steps.stepSummary: When the stream dried up and ה׳ saw the world was suffering, He sent אליהו to צרפת.
steps.simpleTranslation: After a while the stream dried up, since there was no rain. Once ה׳ saw there was suffering in the world, it says: ה׳ told אליהו, get up and go to צרפת.
steps.whatsHappening: The drought now reaches אליהו's own stream. The גמרא explains that ה׳ sent him to צרפת because He saw the world suffering. This sets up the next story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא adds a reason behind the move to צרפת‎: ה׳ saw the suffering the drought caused. This prepares for the events in צרפת, which lead to the key to rain going back to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: To צרפת, a town where אליהו was sent

phrases.english: "And it came to pass after some days
phrases.notes: מלכים א 17:7

phrases.english: that the stream dried up,
because there was no rain in the land."
Once He saw
phrases.notes: The one who "saw" is ה׳.

phrases.english: that there was suffering in the world,
it is written: "And the word of ה׳ came to him, saying:
phrases.notes: מלכים א 17:8–9

phrases.english: Arise, go to Zarephath."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story forward from נחל כרית to צרפת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ saw the world suffering and sent אליהו to צרפת.

steps.title: The boy gets sick and אליהו asks for the key to תחיית המתים
steps.stepSummary: The landlady's son fell sick, and אליהו prayed to be given the key to תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says: after these events, the son of the woman who owned the house became sick. אליהו prayed that he be given the key to bringing the dead back to life.
steps.whatsHappening: In צרפת the son of the woman hosting אליהו becomes sick. אליהו prays to receive the key to תחיית המתים. This sets up Heaven's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו already holds the key to rain. Now he asks for a second key, the key to bringing the dead back to life. That request leads directly to the key to rain being taken back.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman who owned the house, אליהו's host
Bringing the dead back to life

phrases.english: And it is written: "And it came to pass after these matters
phrases.notes: מלכים א 17:17

phrases.english: that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became sick."
He prayed
that they give him
the key to the resurrection of the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story in צרפת, where אליהו was just sent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו asked for the key to תחיית המתים while still holding the key to rain.

steps.title: Heaven: give back the key to rain, take this one
steps.stepSummary: Heaven answers that three keys are not given to a messenger. אליהו must return the key to rain to receive the key to תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: three keys are not handed to a messenger: birth, rain, and bringing the dead back to life. People will say the student has two keys and the Master only one! Bring this one and take that one.
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven answers אליהו's request. He cannot hold two of the three special keys, so he must trade the key to rain for the key to תחיית המתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally ה׳ keeps these three keys for Himself. If אליהו held two of them, it would look as if the student had more than the Master. So the trade is the way the key to rain goes back to ה׳.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three keys ה׳ normally keeps for Himself: birth, rain, and תחיית המתים. אליהו had to give back rain in order to receive תחיית המתים.

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: "They" means Heaven answering אליהו.

phrases.english: Three keys were not handed over to an agent:
of a woman in childbirth, and of rain,
and of the resurrection of the dead.
People will say: two are in the hand of the student
and one is in the hand of the Master!
Bring this one and take that one.
phrases.notes: Bring back the key to rain, and take the key to bringing the dead back to life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ שָׁלֹשׁ מַפְתְּחוֹת לֹא נִמְסְרוּ לְשָׁלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אליהו's request in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A messenger cannot hold two of the three keys, so אליהו must return the key to rain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the rain came back even though אליהו had sworn it would not fall.

steps.title: The פסוק showing the rain returned
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק where ה׳ says He will give rain proves that the key to rain went back to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "Go, appear before אחאב, and I will give rain."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to prove that the key to rain was now back with ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק‎, ה׳ Himself says "I will give rain", not אליהו. That shows the key had been returned to ה׳.

phrases.english: As it is written: "Go, appear before Ahab,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:1

phrases.english: and I will give rain."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 29 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the key to rain was returned to ה׳.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 18:1, where ה׳ says "I will give rain".

steps.title: A parable: the man who slammed his door and lost his key
steps.stepSummary: A Galilean taught before רב חסדא that אליהו is like a man who slammed his door shut and lost his key.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain Galilean taught before רב חסדא: what is אליהו's story like? It is like a man who slammed his door shut and lost his key.
steps.whatsHappening: A teacher from the Galil gives a parable to sum up what happened to אליהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו shut the rain off, like slamming a door. Then he lost the key to rain, so he could not open it again himself. The parable sums up the whole episode.

phrases.english: A certain Galilean taught
before Rav Chisda:
A parable of Elijah:
to what is the matter comparable?
To a man who slammed his door
and lost his key.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַשׁ הַהוּא גָּלִילָאָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the story of the key to rain with a parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו shut the rain and then lost control of its key.

steps.title: רבי יוסי begins a teaching about אליהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי taught in ציפורי, opening with the words "אבא אליהו". The teaching continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי taught in ציפורי: Father אליהו...
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins here. רבי יוסי starts speaking about אליהו, and the rest of his words continue in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only the opening line. It sets up רבי יוסי's statement, which comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: Tzippori, a city in the Galil
"Father אליהו", a loving way of referring to אליהו

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei taught in Tzippori:
Father Elijah

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching about אליהו after the parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The opening of רבי יוסי's teaching about אליהו, which continues afterward.
